title: Pseudo-coherence is invariant under nilpotent quotient
statement: Let $R'\to R$ be a surjective map of commutative rings whose kernel is a nilpotent ideal. For $K'\in D(R')$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $K=K'\otimes_{R'}^L R$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $K'$ is pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Set $A=R'$ and $I=\ker(A\to R)$, and choose $N\geq1$ with $I^N=0$. Identify $A/I$ with $R$ by sending the class of $a$ to its image: this is well-defined, injective by the definition of $I$, and surjective by the hypothesis. Hence the scalar reductions below are exactly the derived reduction $K$ in the statement.

Assume $K'$ is pseudo-coherent. By [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] choose a bounded-above complex $F^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules representing it. Every term is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so $F^\bullet$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the category with one object and only its identity morphism, with the identity covering. A presheaf on this category is just its value at that object, and the identity-cover sheaf condition imposes no extra restriction. Thus a ring sheaf is a ring and a module sheaf is a module; morphisms, complexes, cohomology, and tensor products are evaluated at that object. Consequently the K-flat computation in clause (2) gives: $K$ is represented by the termwise tensor complex $F^\bullet\otimes_A R$. A basis of each term tensors to the same finite basis over $R$, and zero terms above the bound stay zero. This is a bounded-above finite free model, so the pseudo-coherence definition gives the forward implication.

Conversely assume $K$ is pseudo-coherent. Its definition gives a bounded-above complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules representing it. Its terms are projective by [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-projective-complex-lift] to $A,I,C=K'$ and $E^\bullet$, using the given derived reduction identification and $I^N=0$. Obtain a bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of projective $A$-modules representing $K'$ and an isomorphism of complexes $P^\bullet/IP^\bullet\cong E^\bullet$. In particular every $P^i/IP^i$ has a finite basis. No pseudo-coherence of $K'$ has been assumed in this lifting step. The quotient and tensor descriptions agree degreewise by the mutually inverse maps $p\otimes\bar a\mapsto\overline{ap}$ and $\bar p\mapsto p\otimes1$; these commute with the differentials since those are $A$-linear.

Fix a degree $i$ and choose the finite basis of $P^i/IP^i$ supplied by the isomorphism with $E^i$. Lift its $r_i$ basis vectors to $P^i$, and let $u:A^{\oplus r_i}\to P^i$ send the standard basis to those lifts. Its quotient map modulo $I$ is an isomorphism, hence surjective. Nilpotent Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] makes $u$ surjective even though $P^i$ is not yet known finite. Thus the chosen lifts generate $P^i$.

Projectivity, in its lifting-along-surjections form [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], supplies a section $s:P^i\to A^{\oplus r_i}$ of $u$. Put $T=\ker(u)$. The explicit decomposition $v=(v-su(v))+su(v)$ identifies $A^{\oplus r_i}$ with $T\oplus P^i$. Multiplication by $I$ respects this decomposition, so its quotient is $(T/IT)\oplus(P^i/IP^i)$, and the reduced map of $u$ is the projection onto the second factor. That map is an isomorphism by the chosen basis, so $T/IT=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] to $0\to T$ to conclude $T=0$. Hence $u$ is an isomorphism and $P^i$ is finite free of rank $r_i$. This also works when $r_i=0$.

Perform the preceding argument in every degree of the already constructed complex $P^\bullet$. Its terms are now finite free; its differentials, bound, and derived identification with $K'$ were supplied in step 3 and have not been altered. Thus $P^\bullet$ is a bounded-above finite free model for $K'$. By [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], $K'$ is pseudo-coherent, which proves the reverse implication.
